nodes.characterization_summary: TEM image shows Pd nanoparticles uniformly dispersed on the surface of α-Ni(OH)₂ nanosheets while keeping the sheet-like morphology unchanged.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Obviously, the TEM image in Figure 1C unveils that the as-formed Pd nanoparticles are uniformly dispersed on the surface of α-Ni(OH)₂ nanosheets while keeping the sheet-like morphology unchanged after the reduction treatment.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows two distinguishable lattice fringes with interplanar spacings of 0.232 nm and 0.222 nm matching the (200) and (111) planes of α-Ni(OH)₂ and Pd, respectively, indicative of the heterointerface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, two distinguishable lattice fringes with interplanar spacings of 0.232 and 0.222 nm can be well observed from the high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image in Figure 1D, matching with the (200) and (111) planes of α-Ni(OH)₂ and Pd, respectively, indicative of the heterointerface between them.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern presents the coexistence of (110), (300) and (204) planes of α-Ni(OH)₂ together with (111) and (200) planes of Pd.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Also, the selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern in Figure 1E presents the coexistence of (110), (300) and (204) planes of α-Ni(OH)₂ together with (111) and (200) planes of Pd.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM image confirms the desirable decoration of Pd nanoparticles on the surface of α-Ni(OH)₂ nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-angle annular darkfield scanning TEM (HAADF-STEM) image in Figure 1F confirms the desirable decoration of Pd nanoparticles on the surface of nanosheets.

nodes.characterization_summary: Elemental mapping indicates the homogeneous distribution of Ni, Pd, and O elements in Pd-Ni(OH)₂ nanocomposite.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1G presents the corresponding elemental mapping of Pd-Ni(OH)₂ nanocomposite, visually indicating the homogeneous distribution of Ni, Pd, and O elements in such hybrid sample.

nodes.characterization_summary: The atomic ratio of Pd/Ni is determined to be ≈1/58.5.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In addition, the atomic ratio of Pd/Ni is determined to be ≈1/58.5 by the inductively coupled plasma analysis.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD pattern shows only characteristic peaks ascribed to α-Ni(OH)₂ phase (JCPDS card No. 22-0444), mainly because of the low content of Pd nanoparticles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 2A, only characteristic peaks ascribed to α-Ni(OH)₂ phase (JCPDS card No. 22-0444) can be identified in the XRD pattern, mainly because of the low content of Pd nanoparticles in the Pd-N_i(OH)_2 hybrid.

nodes.characterization_summary: UPS shows work function (Eφ) values of 7.17 eV for pure Pd nanoparticles and 3.95 eV for α-Ni(OH)₂ nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the Eφ value for pure Pd nanoparticles is estimated to be 7.17 eV, obviously higher than that for α-Ni(OH)₂ nanosheets (3.95 eV)

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p spectrum shows peaks at ≈855.5 and 872.9 eV corresponding to Ni 2p3/2 and Ni 2p1/2 indicating Ni²⁺ oxidation state; Pd 3d spectrum shows peaks at ≈335.2 and 340.5 eV for Pd⁰. Ni 2p peaks shift to higher binding energy and Pd 3d peaks shift to lower binding energy in Pd-Ni(OH)₂ compared to pure components, indicating electron transfer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the high-resolution Ni 2p spectrum shows two evident peaks located at ≈855.5 and 872.9 eV corresponding respectively to the Ni 2p3/2 and Ni 2p1/2 indicating that the oxidation states of Ni within Pd-N_i(OH)_2 and α-Ni(OH)_2 nanosheets are predominantly +2. As for the Pd 3d spectrum in Figure 2D, both Pd-N_i(OH)_2 and Pd nanoparticles present two prominent peaks at ≈335.2 and 340.5 eV ascribed respectively to the Pd 3d5/2 and Pd 3d3/2, consistent with the characteristic of Pd⁰.

nodes.characterization_summary: XANES spectra at Ni K-edge for Pd-Ni(OH)₂ show positive shift at absorption edge compared to Ni foil and α-Ni(OH)₂, indicating higher Ni valence and lower electron density due to electron transfer to Pd.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the XANES spectra of the Ni K-edge for Pd-N_i(OH)_2 present a positive shift at the absorption edge as compared to Ni foil and α-Ni(OH)₂ nanosheets, which proves that the valence of Ni atoms in Pd-N_i(OH)_2 is slightly higher than that in α-Ni(OH)₂ nanosheets

nodes.characterization_summary: CV curves in non-faradaic region show Pd-Ni(OH)₂ has larger double-layer capacitance (Cdl) than α-Ni(OH)₂, indicating larger electrochemical active surface area.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure S10 (Supporting Information) and Figure 4A, cyclic voltammetry (CV) curves recorded in 1 M KOH at a non-faradaic region and the corresponding double-layer capacitance (C_dl) values suggest that the Pd-Ni(OH)_2 electrode has a larger electrochemical active surface area than the α Ni(OH)_2 electrode, exposing more active sites to boost the BOR activity.
